contextSummary: Democrats currently look favored in the New Hampshire Senate race because the latest polling shows Chris Pappas ahead of John Sununu, with multiple recent surveys putting him in the lead by about 5 to 8 points. That said, outside spending on the Republican side is substantial and at least one forecast still treats the race as competitive, so the outcome remains sensitive to turnout, undecided voters, and late movement.

headlines.title: New Hampshire Senate Race: 5 Takeaways From a New Poll
headlines.summary: A new NYT/Siena poll found Chris Pappas leading John Sununu 50% to 45% among likely voters. The result suggested a modest but meaningful Democratic edge in a race that remains closely watched.
headlines.relevanceExplanation: This is one of the strongest recent indicators that Democrats are currently ahead, and it directly raises the likelihood of a Democratic win.

headlines.title: Poll shows Pappas opens lead in New Hampshire Senate race
headlines.summary: The UNH Survey Center reported Pappas at 50% and Sununu at 42% in its latest Granite State poll. The poll added to a run of recent surveys showing Democratic improvement.
headlines.relevanceExplanation: A second recent poll showing Pappas ahead supports the view that Democrats have momentum rather than a single-poll anomaly.

headlines.title: New Pappas vs. Sununu, Shaheen vs. DiLorenzo poll shows close races in New Hampshire
headlines.summary: Coverage of the UNH survey said Pappas had reversed an August polling deficit and now led Sununu 50% to 42%. The report also noted that Sununu’s favorability remains underwater.
headlines.relevanceExplanation: The shift from a prior Sununu lead to a Pappas lead suggests momentum is moving toward Democrats, which is favorable for their win probability.

headlines.title: Democrats leading in Michigan, New Hampshire Senate ...
headlines.summary: The Hill reported Pappas ahead 50% to 45% in the New Hampshire Senate contest. Both candidates were described as holding net-negative favorability ratings.
headlines.relevanceExplanation: Even with unfavorable personal ratings on both sides, Democrats still holding the lead suggests their baseline position is stronger in the race right now.

headlines.title: Election 2026: New Hampshire Senate
headlines.summary: Rasmussen found Pappas with an 11-point lead over Sununu in a likely-voter survey, 45% to 34%. The poll was conducted earlier in September and showed a much wider Democratic advantage than some later polls.
headlines.relevanceExplanation: This earlier poll reinforces the broader pattern of Democratic strength, although the gap is larger than in more recent surveys, so it should be treated cautiously.

headlines.title: New Hampshire U.S. Senate Election 2026: Latest Polls
headlines.summary: The NYT polling average page shows several recent surveys clustered in Pappas’s favor, including a Trafalgar poll at Pappas +7, NYT/Siena at +5, UNH at +8, and InsiderAdvantage at +8. The aggregation indicates a consistent Democratic edge in late September.
headlines.relevanceExplanation: A cluster of recent polls all pointing the same direction is one of the clearest measurable signals that Democrats are favored to win.

headlines.title: New Hampshire Senate Fundraising
headlines.summary: The fundraising tracker rates the race as a toss-up and estimates roughly $52.16 million has been spent over the last two years. It also notes that Republicans have slightly outspent Democrats overall in the race.
headlines.relevanceExplanation: Heavy Republican spending can narrow the race and keep it competitive, which modestly lowers Democratic certainty despite the polling lead.
